==English==
{{wp}}
[[File:Hexahedron.svg|thumb|A cube]]

===Etymology 1===
From {{uder|en|fro|cube|}}, from {{uder|en|la|cubus}}, from {{uder|en|grc|κύβος|}}.

{{displaced|ang|tæfel}} ("cube, die, game with dice or tables").

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|kyo͞ob|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/kjuːb/}}
* {{enPR|kyo͞ob|a=US}}, {{IPA|en|/kjub/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-cube.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|uːb|s=1}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|geometry}} A [[regular]] [[polyhedron]] having six identical square faces.
#: {{ux|en|When the math teacher is teaching the class about '''cubes''', he asks them to imagine a cardboard box whose width, length, and height are all the same.}}
# Any object more or less in the form of a cube.
#: {{hypo|en|sugar cube|stock cube}}
#: {{ux|en|A: One '''cube''' or two? B: Oh, no sugar for me, thanks.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q861555}} {{lb|en|mathematics}} The third [[power]] of a [[number]], [[value]], [[term]] or expression.
#: {{ant|en|cube root<id:Q1774143>}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''cube''' of 2 is 8.}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''cube''' of 0.5 is 0.125.}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} A [[data structure]] consisting of a [[three-dimensional]] [[array]]; a [[data cube]].
# A {{w|Rubik's cube}} style puzzle, not necessarily in the shape of a cube.
# {{senseid|en|Q2140397}} {{lb|en|informal|automotive}} {{clipping of|en|cubic inch<id:Q2140397><alt:cubic inch(es)>}}.
#: {{ux|en|As if the 383 weren't already a roaring beast, in 1972 they bored it out some more, bringing it up to 400 '''cubes'''. This 400-'''cube''' monster could launch a land yacht like the Plymouth Fury from zero to sixty in under ten seconds.}}
# {{senseid|en|uncool person}} {{lb|en|1950s|_|slang|dated}} An extremely socially [[conventional]] or [[conservative]] person, more so than even a [[square]].

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|arithmetic}} To raise to the third power; to determine the result of multiplying by itself twice.
#: {{ux|en|Three '''cubed''' can be written as 3<sup>3</sup>, and equals twenty-seven.}}
#* {{RQ:Beckett Watt|text=From this severe trial Mr. Nackybal emerged with distinction, having in his '''cubing''' made only twenty-five slight mistakes out of the forty-six cubes demanded, and in his rooting, out of the fifty-three extractions propounded, committed a mere matter of four trifling errors!}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To form into the shape of a cube.
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cut into cubes.
#: {{syn|en|dice}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Cube''' the ham right after adding the curry to the rice.}}
# {{sid|en|Rubik's cube}} {{lb|en|intransitive}} To use a [[Rubik's cube]].
#: {{ux|en|He likes to '''cube''' now and then.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Yu-chen Li|quotee=Lin Yangxi|title=Specialist coaches and hours of practice a day: the making of China’s six-year-old Rubik’s Cube prodigy|date=2026-09-26|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/26/dream-come-true-six-year-old-rubiks-cube-world-record|author2=Amy Hawkins|passage=“She has gained a lot of love and attention through '''cubing'''.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261018142511/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/26/dream-come-true-six-year-old-rubiks-cube-world-record|archivedate=18 October 2026}}

===Pronunciation===

* {{rhymes|en|iːtʃ|s=1}}
* {{hyph|en|teach}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*deyḱ-}}
{{ety|en|id=instruct|:inh|enm:techen|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|techen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tǣċan|t=to show, declare, demonstrate; teach, instruct, train; assign, prescribe, direct; warn; persuade}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*taikijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*taikijaną|t=to show}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*deyḱ-|t=to show}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sco|tech}}, {{m|sco|teich|t=to teach}}, {{cog|de|zeigen|t=to show, point out}}, {{m|de|zeihen|t=accuse, blame}}, {{cog|got|𐌲𐌰𐍄𐌴𐌹𐌷𐌰𐌽|t=to announce, declare, tell, show, display}}, {{cog|la|dīcō|t=speak, say, tell}}, {{cog|grc|δείκνυμι|t=show, point out, explain, teach}}, {{cog|sa|दिशति|t=to point out, show, tell, teach}}. More at {{l|en|token}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb|~es|~ing|taught}}

# {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To [[pass]] on [[knowledge]] to.
#: {{syn|en|educate|instruct}}
#: {{ux|en|Can you '''teach''' me to sew?  Can you '''teach''' sewing to me?}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|stative}} To [[pass]] on [[knowledge]] generally, especially as one's profession; to act as a [[teacher]].
#: {{ant|en|learn}}
#: {{ux|en|She used to '''teach''' at university.}}
# {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To [[cause]] (someone) to [[learn]] or [[understand]] (something).
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=The humor of my proposition appealed more strongly to Miss Trevor than I had looked for, and from that time forward she became her old self again;{{nb...}}. Now she had come to look upon the matter in its true proportions, and her anticipation of a possible chance of '''teaching''' him a lesson was a pleasure to behold.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=September-October|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/robert-l-dorit Rob Dorit]
|magazine=w:American Scientist|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/5/making-life-from-scratch Making Life from Scratch]
|passage=Deep Blue '''taught''' us a great deal about the power of the human mind precisely because it could not reproduce the intuitive and logical leaps of Kasparov’s mind. A truly synthetic cell, built from scratch or even from preexisting components, will be a cell without ancestry, and it, too, will '''teach''' us a great deal about the underlying complexities of life without actually reproducing them.}}
# {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To [[cause]] to [[know]] the [[disagreeable]] [[consequences]] of some action.
#: {{ux|en|I'll '''teach''' you to make fun of me!}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To show (someone) the way; to [[guide]], [[conduct]]; to [[point]], [[indicate]].
#: {{ux|en|‘The bliss is there’, mumbled the old man and '''taught''' to Heaven.}}
#* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|8.5|2|VI|v|passage=So thus within a whyle as they thus talked the nyghte passed / and the daye shone / and thenne syre launcelot armed hym / and took his hors / and they '''taught''' hym to the Abbaye and thyder he rode within the space of two owrys}}
<!--Prior quote:Than Sir Launcelot armed hym and toke his horse, and so he was '''taughte''' to the abbey.-->

===Alternative forms===

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:ever}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂ey-|id1=life|*perkʷ-}}
From {{der|en|enm|ever}}, from {{der|en|ang|ǣfre}}, originally a phrase whose first element undoubtedly consists of {{cog|ang|ā|t=ever, always}} + {{m|ang|in|t=in}} + an element possibly from {{m|ang|feorh|t=life, existence}} (dative {{m|ang|fēore}}). Compare {{cog|ang|ā tō fēore|t=ever in life}}, {{cog|ang|feorhlīf||life}} from {{af|ang|feorh|līf|t1=life|t2=life|nocat=1}}.

Sense 5 of the adverb was likely formed by association with {{m|en|never}}, which also carries the meaning of ''did not'' in colloquial Singaporean and Malaysian English. Also, compare {{sl|en|zh|[[有]] … [[過]]|tr=yǒu ... guò / jau<sup>5</sup> ... gwo<sup>3</sup>|notext=1|t=has {{...}} before}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɛvə(ɹ)/}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-ever.ogg|a=UK}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-ever.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛvə(ɹ)|s=2}}
* {{hyphenation|en|ev|er}}

===Adverb===
{{en-adv|-}}

# {{lb|en|formal|or|archaic}} [[always|Always]], [[frequently]], [[forever]].
#: {{ux|en|It was '''ever''' thus.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1592|author=w:George Savile, 1st Marquess of Halifax|title=An Advertisement{{...}} concerning Seminary Priests
|passage={{...}} the Lord Treasurer, who '''ever''' secretly feigned himself to be a Moderator and Mollifier of the Catholicks Afflictions {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|IX|passage=“A tight little craft,” was Austin’s invariable comment on the matron;{{nb...}}. ¶ Near her wandered her husband, orientally bland, invariably affable, and from time to time squinting sideways, as usual, in the '''ever'''-renewed expectation that he might catch a glimpse of his stiff, retroussé moustache.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1993
|author=Nancy K. Florida
|title=Javanese Literature in Surakarta Manuscripts: Introduction and manuscripts of the Karaton Surakarta
|publisher=SEAP Publications
|isbn=9780877276036
|page=9
|passage=The library staffs of the Karaton Surakarta's Sasana Pustaka, the Mangku-  nagaran's Reksa Pustaka, and the Museum Radyapustaka were '''ever''' helpful and  generous with their time.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Roman Frydman; Michael D. Goldberg|title=Imperfect Knowledge Economics: Exchange Rates and Risk|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=9780691121604
|passage=As with the rest of macroeconomics, the issues have to be rethought in a way that  makes the '''ever'''-imperfect knowledge of market participants and policymakers an  integral part of the analysis.}}
#* {{quote-web|en|work=BBC Sport|author=Phil McNulty|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58404777|date=8 September 2021|title=Poland 1-1 England|passage={{w|Harry Kane|Kane}} picked up the ball 25 yards out with 18 minutes left before proving he is '''ever''' the opportunist by flashing a dipping swerving drive beyond the deceived {{w|Wojciech Szczesny|Szczesny}}.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260203031903/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58404777|archivedate=3 February 2026}}
